title: change-mitigation-controller-with-economics-aware-undo-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
Build a Change Mitigation Controller and an Economics-Aware Undo Playbook to safely apply and, when necessary, revert config changes that affect batching/caching and serving economics. The controller should be able to: stage changes, run preflight simulations, apply canaries, observe economic & quality signals, and perform deterministic undo operations (snapshots + replay) when guardrails trip.

Goals:
- Prevent large cost regressions from config changes to batching/caching profiles and routing policies.
- Make safety operations deterministic and auditable (snapshots, events, and playbooks).
- Provide an operators-friendly UI/CLI flow for hazard review and manual undos.
- Integrate with Optimize recommendations so suggested config sets can be safely trialed.

Scope:
- Control-plane policy engine that evaluates change safety based on economic thresholds (delta per-token cost, 95th/99th latency, KV cache hit ratio) and quality metrics (eval prompt set pass rate).
- Light-weight node agent to snapshot runtime config and KV/cache state at change time (to enable deterministic undo and faster reconciliation).
- Preflight dry-run harness that replays a sampled traffic stream (or synthetic workload) against new config in an isolated canary env to estimate cost/latency delta.
- Change apply flow: staged shadow apply -> 1% traffic canary -> 5% canary -> ramp -> full apply. Each stage has automated hold/undo predicates.
- Undo playbook: snapshot restore + policy-driven stepwise revert (not blind revert). Keep last-known-good config snapshots for quick reversion and for postmortem analysis.

Acceptance criteria:
- The controller can block or pause an apply automatically when: cost delta > configured threshold, 95th latency increase > configured threshold, KV cache hit ratio drops > configured threshold, or quality eval regression > configured threshold.
- Preflight simulation produces a deterministic estimate of token cost and latency with confidence bounds; estimates must be within ±15% of canary observed values in internal tests.
- Node agent snapshots are captured and can be restored in >90% of test scenarios within target 3 minute window.
- All operations and decisions are logged to our audit pipeline and surfaced in Console change history with links to snapshots and PRs.
- Support for a manual "pause and inspect" checkpoint before full rollout.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Centralized policy engine (control plane) vs fully decentralized per-cluster enforcement: we chose a hybrid. Policy and decision logic live in the control plane to keep rules consistent; small agents on Dedicated/Private nodes perform snapshots, local validation, and apply/undo actions to avoid cross-network latencies and to comply with air-gapped setups.
- Preflight dry-run: full production traffic replay would be ideal but costly; we will sample representative traffic slices (prefix-aware sampling) and a small synthetic burst to stress batching heuristics. This reduces cost while surfacing batching/caching regressions.
- Economic thresholds are configurable per-customer tier: Hosted gets conservative defaults; Dedicated customers can opt into more aggressive trade-offs.
- Strong preference for stepwise undo (restore snapshot + incrementally re-enable features) rather than instant global revert to reduce cross-service instability.

Telemetry & metrics to watch:
- cost.delta.per-hour (expected vs observed), cost.per-token 50/95/99 percentiles
- latency.p50/p95/p99 preflight vs canary vs prod
- kv_cache.hit_ratio and eviction.rate
- batching.size.avg and inference.throughput
- canary.pass_rate and eval.promptset.delta
- change.apply.duration and snapshot.restore.duration

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (weeks 1-3): implement control-plane policy engine, write policy DSL, and build APIs for change staging and audits.
- Phase 2 (weeks 4-6): build node agent for snapshotting and safe apply primitives; integrate with preflight harness.
- Phase 3 (weeks 7-9): wire in Optimize suggestions and implement economic thresholds; run internal dogfood on non-critical models.
- Phase 4 (weeks 10-12): user-facing Console integration (change timeline, "inspect snapshot" UI), beta with selected customers.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for policy DSL evaluation and threshold math.
- Integration tests: simulated traffic replay against canary infra, fault injections for agent network partitions, snapshot corruption simulation.
- Chaos tests: random delayed snapshot restores and partial application to validate idempotency.
- Post-deploy runbook: automated diagnosis step that links to top-3 contributing signals and suggests the undo playbook step to run.

Dependencies & integration points:
- Optimize suggestion engine for initial recommended config sets (consume recommendations API).
- Console for change history and manual inspection UI.
- Audit/logging pipeline for event persistence (compliance).
- Billing/Cost metrics infra to compute cost.delta.* metrics in near-real-time.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- What is the exact snapshot format for cache/KV state that is both space-efficient and restorable across minor runtime versions? (R&D spike planned).
- Should we add a "simulated revert" stage in preflight that estimates the undo cost (how expensive the revert path is) prior to applying changes?
- Who owns the policies for enterprise customers: central SRE or customer-managed? Proposal: central SRE with customer override flags for Dedicated/private installs.

Milestones:
- 2026-02-26: policy DSL v0 done (blocking: DSL schema review)
- 2026-03-05: node agent snapshot prototype (blocking: agent permission model)
- 2026-03-20: preflight harness integration test stable
